text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"more developed multi-sentence argument about hearing multiple voices","quality":"idea development","description":"This captures how fully an essay expands and supports its main point with connected explanation."},{"evidence":"uses transitions like \"However,\" \"For example,\" and \"Sometimes\"","quality":"cohesion","description":"This captures how smoothly an essay links ideas across sentences and paragraphs."},{"evidence":"sustained discussion of advice affecting motivation and behavior","quality":"relevance of support","description":"This captures how consistently an essay stays focused on elaborating its central claim rather than repeating it."},{"evidence":"sentences such as \"two brain is better than one\" and \"it would impact them in a positive or a negative way depends on who they ask\"","quality":"syntactic control","description":"This captures greater control of sentence structure, including more complex and varied constructions."},{"evidence":"words like \"motivated,\" \"convinced,\" \"impact,\" and \"negatively\"","quality":"vocabulary range","description":"This captures broader and more precise word choice for expressing abstract ideas."},{"evidence":"fewer repeated template phrases than B","quality":"redundancy control","description":"This captures how much an essay avoids unnecessary repetition and formulaic restatement."}]}
